    Changelog

    Source: NEWS.md

    scimagR 0.2.0

    Spinal Cord Toolbox wrappers

    • The wrappers support SCT 7: sct_segment_sc() and sct_segment_lesion() read the installed version from sct_version and call sct_deepseg spinalcord / sct_deepseg lesion_sci_t2 (SCT >= 7.0) or sct_deepseg -task ... (SCT 6). SCT 7 given -task printed a note and exited with status 0, so the wrappers used to report success without an output file.
    • All wrappers now check that SCT wrote the expected file and return NA with a warning when it did not. sct_segment_lesion() also returns NA with a warning when the lesion mask cannot be copied to output.
    • The wrappers return the files SCT actually writes: sct_segment_lesion() saves the SCIsegV2 lesion mask under output and the cord mask next to it as *_sc_seg.nii.gz (SCT appends _lesion_seg and _sc_seg to the name given with -o); sct_label_vertebrae() returns <segmentation>_labeled.nii.gz, the vertebral level file that sct_process_segmentation() needs (it used to return a *_labels-disc.nii.gz path that SCT never writes); sct_analyze_lesion() returns the *_analysis.xlsx (SCT 6.5 and later) or *_analysis.xls (SCT 6.4) spreadsheet instead of a non-existent CSV.
    • sct_segment_sc() and sct_segment_lesion() pass qc_dir to sct_deepseg -qc. sct_generate_qc() defaults to the valid sct_qc process "sct_deepseg_sc" (the former default "sct_deepseg" is mapped to it) and gains lesion and plane for lesion reports.
    • sct_process_segmentation() gains vert and perlevel to aggregate per vertebral level; its documentation now says that by default SCT averages over all slices and leaves the VertLevel column empty.
    • Arguments passed to SCT are shell-quoted, so paths with spaces work.

    Pipeline, DICOM and registry

    • sci_run_pipeline() is documented as a planner: it runs no tool and reports every step as pending. sci_pipeline_status() recognises the SCT output names, no longer counts a lesion mask as a cord segmentation, and always returns its documented columns.
    • extract_dicom_metadata() takes pat_id from the folder name, as documented, and no longer exports the PatientID header, which could hold a hospital number and broke the paths convert_batch() builds.
    • create_registry() recodes the DICOM modality "MR" to "MRT", so registries built from extracted metadata pass validate_registry(), and warns about patients without a trauma date.
    • create_registry() matches trauma and surgery dates to patients by ID text. A numeric pat_id (e.g. from folders named 1, 2, …) used to pick the dates by position, so patients could silently get another patient’s trauma date, days since trauma and phase. create_registry() and validate_registry() read pat_id and session from a CSV as text.
    • convert_dcm2niix() raises an error when ‘dcm2niix’ fails.
    • anonymize_dicom() documents exactly which tags it changes and that it is not a full DICOM PS3.15 de-identification.
    • Two synthetic DICOM slices (inst/extdata/dicom/, made by data-raw/make_example_dicom.py) let the DICOM examples and tests run where ‘pydicom’ or ‘dcm2niix’ is installed.

    Metrics and plots

    • compute_mscc(), compute_compression_ratio() and compute_csa_ratio() are vectorised (they failed on vectors, e.g. inside dplyr::mutate()) and cite their definitions (Fehlings et al. 1999; Ogino et al. 1983). Arguments of length 1 are recycled; any other length mismatch is an error instead of being recycled silently.
    • classify_phase() returns NA with a warning for negative days, and classify_artifact() for grades that are not whole numbers.
    • The phase, artefact and modality scales list legend entries in palette order; plot_coverage() explains the grade numbers in a caption; plot_forest() no longer uses the deprecated geom_errorbarh().

    Documentation

    • Examples no longer use \dontrun{}: each wrapper has an example that runs without the external tool, and the tool calls are in \donttest{} behind check_sct(), check_dcm2niix() or check_pydicom().
    • The getting-started and pipeline vignettes run their tool-free code on synthetic data; the SCT vignette describes the output files.
    • British English throughout; citation metadata name the author R. Heller; grouped pkgdown reference index.

    Other changes

    • sci_run_pipeline() no longer reports steps as complete without running them. It returns the step plan with status "pending" and the function that performs each step; the vignettes and README describe it that way.
    • Prepared the package for a first CRAN submission.
    • theme_sci() now defaults to base_family = "" (the device’s sans-serif font). The previous default "Arial" made every plot fail on the base pdf() device; pass base_family = "Arial" to keep the old look on devices that can use system fonts.
    • Examples now run on bundled or synthetic data for all functions that do not need external software (registry, coverage, quality control, plotting, export and project scaffolding).
    • DESCRIPTION: title without “in R”, expanded description with a reference for the Spinal Cord Toolbox, optional SystemRequirements, Language, pkgdown URL and the maintainer’s ORCID.
    • Documented the colour palettes’ format.

    scimagR 0.1.0

    • Standardise the named v5 package logo across README, documentation pages and available application headers, with matching light and dark artwork.

    • Initial release.

    • SCT interface: R wrappers for spinal cord segmentation, lesion segmentation, vertebral labelling, and parameter extraction.

    • DICOM tools: metadata extraction, anonymisation, batch NIfTI conversion.

    • SCI metrics: MSCC, compression ratio, CSA ratio, phase classification, artefact grading.

    • Registry management: creation, validation, coverage matrix visualisation.

    • QC system: segmentation QC logging, evaluability filtering, exclusion tracking.

    • Visualisation: publication-ready theme, SCI-specific palettes and scales, standard plot types (violin-box, spaghetti, forest).

    • Pipeline orchestration: idempotent multi-step processing with resume support.

    • Project scaffolding: sci_create_project() for workflowr-based SCI studies.
